- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending up, cap the rise at 1–2% above recent mean to avoid false momentum.  
- If forecast overshoots true value by >3% in early days of the 30d horizon, apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.25) and forecast is smooth, introduce a 1–3% smoothing penalty to reduce overfitting to recent noise.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3–5 days, apply a 1–2% downward bias correction to reflect mean reversion toward prior range.  
- For forecasts with high variance in early days (e.g., >10% from mean), reduce confidence in later days by applying a 1–3% decay factor to avoid horizon drift.
